title: Principality of Ryazan
capsule: The Principality of Ryazan split off from the Chernigov lands in the late 11th century under a cadet branch of the Rurikids, with its capital at Old Ryazan on the Oka River guarding the southeastern steppe frontier of Rus'. Chronically at war with the Cumans and its rival princes of Vladimir-Suzdal, Ryazan nonetheless prospered as a river-trade center until December 1237, when it became the first Rus' principality struck by Batu Khan's Mongol invasion; after a five-day siege its capital was burned and its population massacred. Prince Ingvar Ingorevich salvaged what remained of the principality in the invasion's aftermath, ruling from a new seat as Ryazan began its long existence as a Mongol tributary.
